doc_verification.detail: Reachability: no doc_preflight.json sidecar existed anywhere in the tree, so live fetch was attempted; WebFetch was blocked twice at the domain-safety layer (api.qdrant.tech, network restriction — domain_blocked event on that channel) and an MCP web-reader fallback channel fetched the page successfully (rendered page + .md version both read), so the URL is verified reachable with full content. Version: page selector and URL both v1.18.x, target v1.18.0 — major.minor matched. Content: the page documents `actions` (required) as 'list of object or object or object' with exactly three single-key variants (CreateAliasOperation/DeleteAliasOperation/RenameAliasOperation, each inner field required) and their single-key cURL examples — the schema face the claim attacks is real; BUT the page prose never states 'exactly one operation key per element', documents only the 200 response (in-tree docs/redoc/v1.18.x/openapi.json adds only a generic default/4XX error bucket, no explicit 400 for malformed shapes), and the cited constraint's 404/500 clauses are not visible in the fetched page prose (they exist in raw_knowledge.json pipeline capture and as the source's runtime 404 check). In-tree formal schema is anyOf (permissive: a multi-key element matches >=1 variant and is formally valid), not oneOf. Endpoint: registry aliases+update = POST /collections/aliases with actions required and response result:boolean — exactly what the script called and observed.

rest, same-log: probe[actions-empty-array] -> status=200 ... 'OK: empty batch 200 no-op, zero state change' (L21-23) — the oracle pre-accepted empty batch as documented-tolerable

grpc face: live comparison unobtainable in this REST-only sandbox — face_unavailable; in-source proto (lib/api/src/grpc/proto/collections.proto L813-819) defines message AliasOperations { oneof action {...} } so a double-key element is structurally unrepresentable on gRPC (REST/JSON face only)

http_semantics.note: Strictly stronger than a business error code: the schema-invalid request (element carrying two operation keys) returned HTTP 200 with a SUCCESS envelope {"result":true,"status":"ok"} and a real state mutation — no error signal of any kind; the client's delete_alias instruction was silently discarded.

contract_grounding.assertion_text_quoted: returns 200 ok; 404 on create_alias of a missing collection; 404/500 on delete_alias of an unknown alias
contract_grounding.note: Violates-declaration self-check applied: the observed phenomenon (200 + result:true on a shape-invalid element) does not contradict the quoted text — after serde untagged first-match deserialization the effective batch was a create_alias on an EXISTING collection, which the assertion's own text says returns 200; no missing-collection create and no unknown-alias delete was involved, so the 404/500 clauses are untouched. The norm the claim actually attacks (element-key exclusivity, oneOf per element) is OUTSIDE this constraint's domain — it is carried by the co-anchored registry face (endpoint_registry aliases+update: parameter type 'array[create_alias|delete_alias|rename_alias]', request_required_paths actions[].{create_alias,delete_alias,rename_alias}), and even that face is formally permissive: in-tree OpenAPI uses anyOf (docs/redoc/v1.18.x/openapi.json L11109) and the published page documents no 400 for this endpoint. Constraint citation should be read as the shape face, not the status-code face. The surviving behavioral hazard for the auditor: half of a client's element-level instructions silently executed, half silently dropped, zero diagnostics.

source_grounding.call_chain_traced: actix Json<ChangeAliasesOperation> extractor (collections_api.rs:180-196, no validator extractor, no .validate() call) -> serde deserializes actions:Vec<AliasOperations> via #[serde(untagged)] (collection_meta_ops.rs:81): variants tried in declaration order, CreateAlias matches the double-key element first and the sibling delete_alias key is silently discarded (untagged enums cannot carry deny_unknown_fields, and no variant struct sets it either) -> dispatcher.submit_collection_meta_op(CollectionMetaOperations::ChangeAliases) -> toc update_aliases (toc/collection_meta_ops.rs:307-336) iterates the already-deserialized variants: CreateAlias applied (alias_lock.insert:319; validate_collection_exists:316 is the documented 404 check), DeleteAlias arm never runs because the delete instruction never existed post-deserialization. This exactly reproduces the observed state leak (alias bau29c6e20d7y created, delete half dropped, 200 true). The same enum DOES reject unknown keys / wrong types with 400 'data did not match any variant of untagged enum AliasOperations' (log L25-35) — so validation exists for variant *selection* but is absent for variant-key *exclusivity within one element*. gRPC face: proto oneof makes the double-key shape unrepresentable there. tests/openapi/test_alias.py covers alias CRUD ordering only; no test pins multi-key element behavior.
source_grounding.verification_detail: No element-key-exclusivity validation exists anywhere on the REST path (handler, deserializer, or apply loop) — that specific validation is absent, which mechanically explains the observation. Two honesty caveats for the auditor: (1) no explicit by-design declaration exists either (no comment/docstring/maintainer citation saying multi-key tolerance is intended — by_design_in_source therefore NOT supportable; the closest comment '*Operation wrapper structure is only required for better OpenAPI generation' L32 concerns wrapper naming, not key exclusivity); (2) the requirement itself is only implied: the published page and in-tree OpenAPI use anyOf without additionalProperties:false, so a double-key element is formally schema-valid — the 'invalid shape' premise rests on the oneOf-per-element reading (registry parameter type array[create_alias|delete_alias|rename_alias] + request_required_paths) rather than on an explicit documented rejection promise.

mundane_explanation.surviving: Mechanical cause confirmed in source: serde untagged first-match + no deny_unknown_fields silently discards all but the first variant key of an element (lib/storage/src/content_manager/collection_meta_ops.rs:81). Whether this tolerance is intended is undetermined: no explicit by-design declaration found, and the formal schema face (anyOf) is permissive — auditor must weigh the silent half-application of client instructions against a schema that never explicitly forbids multi-key elements.
